title: Granola adds free dictation on the Mac, in any app
friendlyTitle: Granola can now type what you say, for free, on a Mac
summary: Granola, the meeting-notes app, added voice typing on 29 October. On a Mac, holding the Fn key and speaking produces cleaned-up text in the app that has focus, including notes, prompts, email, and messages. Granola says the words are unlimited and free. iOS and Windows are planned, not shipping yet.
friendlySummary: Granola, an app that writes meeting notes, added voice typing on 29 October. On a Mac, you hold the Fn key and speak. It cleans up the words and puts them in whatever app you are using, including notes, prompts, email, and messages. Granola says there is no word limit and no charge. iPhone and Windows versions are planned, not available yet.
whyItMatters: Meeting notes and dictation are collapsing into the same product. Wispr added notes to a dictation app; Granola has now added dictation to a notes app. The practical difference is where the audio goes and what it is allowed to clean up. A tool that rewrites your speech before it lands in an email is useful, and it is also another place a spoken aside can be stored.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Note-taking apps and dictation apps are starting to do the same jobs. The practical question is where the recording goes, and how much the tool rewrites before the text lands in an email. That rewrite can save time. It is also another place a spoken aside can be stored.
